facts.statement: Argentinian paleontologist Diego Pol discovered the skeleton of Eoabelisaurus near the village of Cerro Cóndor in Chubut Province in 2009.
facts.quote: In 2009, Argentinian paleontologist Diego Pol discovered the skeleton of a theropod near the village of Cerro Cóndor in Chubut Province.

facts.statement: The species Eoabelisaurus mefi was named and described in 2012 by Diego Pol and Oliver Rauhut.
facts.quote: In 2012, based on these remains, the type species Eoabelisaurus mefi was named and described by Pol and his German colleague Oliver Rauhut.

facts.statement: Eoabelisaurus lived during the Lower Jurassic in the Cañadón Asfalto Basin of Argentina.
facts.quote: Eoabelisaurus () is a genus of abelisauroid theropod dinosaur from the Lower Jurassic Cañadón Asfalto Formation of the Cañadón Asfalto Basin in Argentina, South America.

facts.statement: Eoabelisaurus was a bipedal carnivore estimated to be between 5.8 and 6.5 meters long.
facts.quote: It was a bipedal carnivore that was estimated to have reached 6 - 6.5 m in length, although a comprehensive analysis of abelisaur size conducted in 2016 yielded a size estimate of 5.8 m.

facts.statement: Eoabelisaurus is estimated to have weighed between 730 and 800 kilograms.
facts.quote: It is estimated to have weighed up to 730 - 800 kg.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen dates to the Middle-Late Toarcian, approximately 179 to 178 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, MPEF PV 3990, was uncovered in a layer of the Cañadón Asfalto Formation, a lacustrine deposit dating originally from the Aalenian-Bajocian, roughly 170 million years old, yet a recent advanced zircon datation constrained its age to the Middle-Late Toarcian (179-178 million years).

facts.statement: Parts of the skull and anterior presacrals were partially destroyed by erosion before discovery.
facts.quote: The skull and anterior presacrals were also exposed at the time of discovery and had been partially been destroyed by erosion.

facts.statement: A fragment of the right maxilla shows that the interdental plates were fused but not striated.
facts.quote: From the material known of the snout, only a small fragment of the right maxilla has been recovered and shows that the interdental plates are fused, but not striated.

facts.statement: The skull roof of Eoabelisaurus was not notably thickened and lacked cranial ornamentation.
facts.quote: The skull roof is not notably thickened and no cranial ornamentation is present.

facts.statement: The humeri of Eoabelisaurus are poorly preserved but exhibit primitive characteristics.
facts.quote: Both humeri from the known material are poorly preserved, but show primitive characters.

facts.statement: The radius and ulna were short, with the ulna possessing a large olecranon process.
facts.quote: The radius and ulna are short and the ulna has a large olecranon process.

facts.statement: The hand was very foreshortened, retained four digits, and had short metacarpals.
facts.quote: The manus is very foreshortened, retains four digits, and has short metacarpals.

facts.statement: The non-terminal manual phalanges were roughly as long as wide without constriction, while the manual claws were reduced.
facts.quote: The non-terminal manual phalanges are about as long as wide and lack any constriction between the articular ends, and manual unguals are reduced.

facts.statement: The reduced limb proportions of Eoabelisaurus demonstrate that it was a primitive abelisaurid.
facts.quote: It is these reduced limb proportions that demonstrate Eoabelisaurus was indeed a primitive abelisaurid.

facts.statement: The original describers assigned Eoabelisaurus to the basalmost position in the family Abelisauridae.
facts.quote: Eoabelisaurus was assigned to the basalmost position in Abelisauridae by its describers.

facts.statement: In 2018, Rafael Delcourt placed Eoabelisaurus at the base of Ceratosauridae, though he noted the classification was problematic.
facts.quote: In 2018, Rafael Delcourt placed Eoabelisaurus at the basic position within Ceratosauridae, noting that the topology of this genus is still problematic.

facts.statement: Eoabelisaurus represents an unknown stage in abelisaurid evolution, possessing only some cranial modifications and a unique combination of forelimb features.
facts.quote: Eoabelisaurus shows what was previously an unknown stage in the evolution of abelisaurids, having only some of the cranial modifications and a unique combination of features in its forelimbs.

facts.statement: Research suggests the modification of abelisaurid forelimbs occurred in a modular fashion, starting with distal elements like fingers before affecting proximal elements.
facts.quote: The modification of the forelimbs in the evolution of abelisaurids seems to have occurred in a modular fashion, starting with the distal elements such as the fingers, and only later affecting the more proximal elements.

facts.statement: Eoabelisaurus mefi lived approximately 170 million years ago during the Bajocian stage of the Middle Jurassic in what is now South America.
facts.quote: Eoabelisaurus mefi es la única especie conocida del género extinto Eoabelisaurus de dinosaurio terópodo abelisáurido que vivió en el a mediados del período período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 170 millones de años durante el Bajociano, en lo que ahora es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the placement of Eoabelisaurus at the base of Ceratosauridae is well-supported.
facts.quote: However, such classification is not well-supported.

facts.statement: Eoabelisaurus was a bipedal carnivore that likely reached a length of 6.5 meters.
facts.quote: Era un carnívoro bípedo que probablemente alcanzaba 6.5 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: A comprehensive 2016 analysis of abelisaurids estimated Eoabelisaurus to be 5.8 meters long.
facts.quote: aunque un análisis exhaustivo del tamaño de los abelisáuridos realizado en 2016 arrojó una estimación de tamaño de 5,8 metros.

facts.statement: The skull and anterior presacral vertebrae were exposed at discovery and partially destroyed by erosion.
facts.quote: El cráneo y los presacros anteriores también estaban expuestos en el momento del descubrimiento y habían sido parcialmente destruidos por la erosión.

facts.statement: A recovered fragment of the right maxilla shows that interdentary plates are fused but not striated.
facts.quote: Del material conocido del hocico, solo se ha recuperado un pequeño fragmento del maxilar derecho y muestra que las placas interdentales están fusionadas, pero no estriadas.

facts.statement: The posterior skull is high with an oval orbit and an enlarged infratemporal fenestra, similar to other ceratosaurians.
facts.quote: La parte posterior conocida del cráneo es alta, con una órbita ovalada y una fenestra infratemporal ampliada, similar a otros ceratosaurianos.

facts.statement: The skull roof is not notably thickened and lacks cranial ornamentation.
facts.quote: El techo del cráneo no está notablemente engrosado y no hay ornamentación craneal.

facts.statement: The hand is very short, retains four digits, and has short metacarpals.
facts.quote: La mano es muy corta, conserva cuatro dígitos y tiene metacarpianos cortos.

facts.statement: Metacarpal I is approximately half the length of metacarpal II and considerably thinner.
facts.quote: El metacarpiano I tiene aproximadamente la mitad de la longitud del metacarpiano II y es considerablemente más delgado.

facts.statement: Non-terminal manual phalanges are roughly as long as they are wide, lack constriction between articular ends, and manual unguals are reduced.
facts.quote: Las falanges manuales no terminales son aproximadamente tan largas como anchas y carecen de constricción entre los extremos articulares, y se reducen las ungualidades manuales.

facts.statement: The humerus was not reduced, while the ulna and radius shortened, but these do not differ from basal ceratosaurians.
facts.quote: El húmero no se redujo, y el cúbito y el radio se acortaron, pero no difieren de los ceratosaurianos más basales.

facts.statement: Its cervical vertebrae are short and have two pneumatic foramina on each side of the centrum.
facts.quote: sus vértebras cervicales son cortas y tienen dos fuerzas neumáticas a cada lado del centro.

facts.statement: Argentine paleontologist Diego Pol discovered a theropod skeleton near Cerro Cóndor in Chubut province in 2009.
facts.quote: En 2009 el paleontólogo argentino Diego Pol descubrió el esqueleto de un terópodo cerca del pueblo de Cerro Cóndor en la provincia de Chubut.

facts.statement: The type species Eoabelisaurus mefi was named and described in 2012 by Pol and his German colleague Oliver Walter Mischa Rauhut.
facts.quote: En 2012, basándose en este, la especie tipo Eoabelisaurus mefi fue nombrada y descrita por Pol y su colega alemán Oliver Walter Mischa Rauhut.

facts.statement: The genus name combines the Greek word 'eos' meaning 'dawn' with Abelisaurus, referencing its status as an early relative.
facts.quote: El nombre del género combina el término griego ἠώς, (eos), "amanecer", con el nombre Abelisaurus, en referencia a que representa un pariente temprano de este último.

facts.statement: The species name honors the MEF, the Paleontological Egidio Feruglio Museum in Trelew, where Pol works.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie es en honor del MEF, siglas del Museo Paleontológico Egidio Feruglio, ubicado en Trelew, en el que Pol trabaja.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MPEF PV 3990 was found in the Cañadón Asfalto Formation, a lake deposit dating from the Aalenian to Bajocian, about 170 million years ago.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, MPEF PV 3990, fue descubierto es una capa de la Formación Cañadón Asfalto, un depósito lacustre que data de entre el Aaleniense al Bajociano, hace más o menos 170 millones de años.

facts.statement: The specimen consists of an almost complete skeleton with a skull from an adult or subadult individual.
facts.quote: Este consiste en un esqueleto casi completo con el cráneo, de un individuo adulto o subadulto.

facts.statement: The discovery of Eoabelisaurus extended the temporal range of the clade by more than 40 million years into the Middle Jurassic.
facts.quote: Con el descubrimiento de Eoabelisaurus el rango temporal del clado se extendió por más de 40 millones de años en el Jurásico Medio.

facts.statement: Eoabelisaurus was assigned to the family Abelisauridae in a basal position.
facts.quote: Eoabelisaurus fue asignado por sus descriptores a la familia Abelisauridae, en una posición basal.

facts.statement: This would make it the oldest known abelisaurid for forty million years.
facts.quote: Esto lo convertiría, por cuarenta millones de años, en el más antiguo abelisáurido conocido.

facts.statement: The time range for Eoabelisaurus is the Toarcian stage, from 184.2 to 174.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (184.2 to 174.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: These reduced limb proportions demonstrate that Eoabelisaurus was indeed a primitive abelisaurid.
facts.quote: Son estas proporciones de extremidades reducidas que demuestran Eoabelisaurus de hecho era un abelisáurido primitivo.

facts.statement: Eoabelisaurus shows a previously unknown stage in abelisaurid evolution, possessing only some cranial modifications and a unique combination of features in its forelimbs.
facts.quote: Eoabelisaurus muestra lo que antes era una etapa desconocida en la evolución de los abelisáuridos, teniendo solo algunas de las modificaciones craneales y una combinación única de características en sus extremidades anteriores.

facts.statement: Descriptors noted that in cladistic analysis, a difference of a single trait could result in a more basal position within the Abelisauroidea group.
facts.quote: Los descriptores indicaron que en el análisis cladístico una diferencia de un único rasgo podría resultar en una posición inferior en el árbol evolutivo, es decir basal en el grupo Abelisauroidea.
